$comment: AUTHORING PATTERN LIBRARY — NOT a form definition and NOT consumed at runtime. This is copy-paste guidance for authoring docs/specifications/definitions/<form>.definition.json files. It introduces no include/import mechanism: you COPY a snippet into your definition and rename its ids. Every snippet is a valid fragment of the Form Definition schema (docs/specifications/schema/form-definition.schema.json) and every autofill reference uses only vocabulary registered in backend/vocabulary/registry.json (enforced by tests/backend/test_pattern_library.py). Deliberately named patterns.json, NOT *.definition.json, so the vocabulary linter never treats it as a form.
derivedFrom: docs/specifications/definitions/form_03.definition.json (reference implementation) and the 34 specs in docs/specifications/

conventions.fieldPaths: Conditions/constraints reference fields by dotted path: <section_id>.<field_id>, or <section_id>.<group_id>.<child_id>, or <section_id>.<table_id>.<column_id>. Ids must be unique within their scope.
conventions.renameIds: After copying a snippet, keep ids unique within the form. The snippet ids below are canonical names; reuse them verbatim where only one instance exists (e.g. 'signatory', 'addressee'), and suffix them when a form has several (e.g. 'applicant_block' -> keep, but a second party block becomes 'authorised_person').
conventions.labelsVerbatim: Set every label/title/boilerplate text to the words printed on the official form (transcribe from the matching docs/specifications/form_*.md). The snippet text is an example, not authority.
conventions.dropInapplicableAutofill: Delete autofill.sources entries that do not apply to the form you are authoring. Never add a sourceType/key that is not in the registry — the linter will reject the definition.
conventions.globalStrikeoutNote: Note. - Strike out whichever is not applicable.
goldenRules: Invent nothing: only fields printed on the form. An optional line that is struck when N/A is modelled as an optional field, not a yes/no toggle.
No printed 'Dated this...' line on Forms 7, 7A and 30 — do NOT add the date_line pattern there; record signing date at app level instead.
No 'To, The Controller... at' addressee on Form 28 — do NOT add the addressee_section there.
Capture 'Designation' on Forms 7A, 26, 29, 30 (signatory_with_designation); capture the official seal only on Forms 26 and 30.
The office-use header uses 'RQ No.' instead of 'Application No.' on Forms 18 and 18A.
strikeoutChoice fields always carry export.strikeoutUnselected=true; boilerplate always carries export.verbatim=true.
Set the sensitive block on OTP/Aadhaar/photo-ID fields (Form 1, 8A, 18A, 22) — authoring must flag them even though redaction is a runtime concern.

document_skeleton.appliesTo: every form — the starting point for a new definition
document_skeleton.description: The complete top-level document envelope: every required and commonly-used top-level key, the two-column layout convention, the verbatim notes array, and the metadata.printedHeader block a renderer needs to reproduce the centred header. Copy this first, then fill sections[] from the other patterns.
document_skeleton.authorNotes: Replace every <...> placeholder and the form_nn / NN ids with values transcribed from the form's docs/specifications/form_*.md. Set layout.columns to 1 for single-column sectioned forms (1, 18, 18A) and 2 for the two-column row-per-section forms. Delete the placeholder section once you add real ones. fee.model is one of first_schedule | none | stamp_duty | other (Form 27 = none; Form 26 = stamp_duty).

snippet.officialName: <exact official name, transcribed from the form>

layout.notes: Two-column forms: each printed numbered row is one section; section.title is the exact left-column label (including its number); the right-column boilerplate + inputs are that section's fields. Set columns=1 for single-column sectioned forms (e.g. Form 1, 18, 18A).

fields.text: Replace this placeholder with fields composed from the library patterns (iwe_strikeout, applicant_names / applicant_block, inline_blank_clause, truth_declaration, ...), transcribing every printed word and field in printed order.

notes: Note. - Strike out whichever is not applicable.
Transcribe every verbatim footnote, warning and fee note printed on the form.

printedHeader.statute: THE PATENTS ACT, 1970 (39 of 1970) and THE PATENTS RULES, 2003
printedHeader.subject: <SUBJECT AS PRINTED, USUALLY UPPERCASE>

inline_blank_clause.appliesTo: 3, 4, 13, 25, 29 and every form with a fill-in-the-blanks printed sentence
inline_blank_clause.description: The canonical way to model a printed sentence that has fill-in blanks: an ordered sequence of boilerplate text + input fields that all share one presentation.group, so a renderer reconstructs the sentence on a single line — e.g. '(i) that I/We who have made the application for patent number [number] in India, dated [date], [alone/jointly with] ...'.
inline_blank_clause.authorNotes: The load-bearing convention is presentation.group: give every fragment of the same printed sentence the SAME group id (here 'clause_i'). Boilerplate carries the verbatim connective words; input fields carry the blanks. Drop into a section's fields[] in printed order. Rename ids and adjust the boilerplate text to the exact sentence on your form.

snippet.text: (i) that I/We who have made the application for patent number

validation.patternMessage: Expected an IPO application number, e.g. 201811000123 or 1234/DEL/2015.

iwe_strikeout.description: The recurring 'I/We' strike-out that opens most declarations. A single control; later literal 'I/We' occurrences live inside boilerplate and are struck consistently per the global note.
iwe_strikeout.authorNotes: Place first in the opening section, usually sharing a presentation.group with the applicant name so the renderer keeps them on one line.

autofill.derivation: Choose 'I' for a single applicant, 'We' for multiple, from the applicant count in uploaded documents.

strikeout_choice_template.appliesTo: any two-way printed alternative (has/have, is/are, my/our, application/Patent, alone/jointly, same/substantially, Grantee/Patentee, patentee/applicant, applicant/patentee)
strikeout_choice_template.description: Generic single-select whose unchosen option is struck through on export. Replace the option values/labels with the printed alternatives.
strikeout_choice_template.authorNotes: Use for any '<a>/<b>' token. If the token sits inside a printed sentence, give it the same presentation.group as the surrounding boilerplate so it renders inline.

strikeout_alone_jointly.description: 'alone / jointly with' choice; selecting 'jointly' typically makes a joint-applicant field required.
strikeout_alone_jointly.authorNotes: Pair with a joint-applicant field that uses requiredWhen/visibleWhen on this field's value = 'jointly'.

autofill.derivation: 'alone' for a single applicant; 'jointly with' when co-applicants exist.

strikeout_has_have.authorNotes: Usually embedded in an assignment/rights sentence; share the surrounding boilerplate's presentation.group.

applicant_names.appliesTo: 3, 4, 13, 29 (forms that print a single 'Name of the applicant(s)' blank)
applicant_names.description: Name-only, repeatable applicant field. Use when the form prints just the applicant name(s), with address/nationality elsewhere or not at all.
applicant_names.authorNotes: Repeatable so multiple applicants can be listed. Drop the form2/certificate sources on forms where only Form 1 is a plausible origin.

applicant_particulars_composite.appliesTo: 7, 8, 9, 11, 14, 15, 17, 19, 21 (forms that print one blank for 'name, address and nationality')
applicant_particulars_composite.description: A single repeatable blank capturing name, address and nationality together, as several forms print it.
applicant_particulars_composite.authorNotes: Autofill seeds the name only (one field binds one primary key); the author confirms/completes address and nationality in the same blank.

snippet.label: Name, address and nationality of the applicant(s)
snippet.helpText: Full name (family/principal name first), complete address incl postal index no./code and state, and nationality.

applicant_block.appliesTo: 1, 5, 2, 6, 10, 12 (forms with structured name / nationality / address sub-fields, repeated per applicant)
applicant_block.description: A structured, repeatable applicant block with discrete name, nationality and address children — each independently auto-fillable.
applicant_block.authorNotes: Prefer this over the composite where the form prints labelled sub-fields (a) Name (b) Address (c) Nationality. Rename to 'inventor' with inventor autofill for inventor blocks; rename to 'authorised_person' for Form 26's second party.

fields.label: Address
fields.helpText: Complete address incl postal index no./code, state and country.

address_for_service.description: The mandatory 'address for service in India' block that appears on most contentious/prosecution forms.
address_for_service.authorNotes: Statutory requirement that it be an Indian address. Where the form asks for telephone/fax inline, extend the helpText; do not invent separate phone fields unless the form prints them.

snippet.label: Address for service in India
snippet.helpText: Must be an address in India. Include postal index no./code, state, and telephone and fax number(s) where the form asks.

date_line.appliesTo: most forms EXCEPT 7, 7A, 30 (which print no date line)
date_line.description: The 'Dated this __ day of __ 20__' date field.
date_line.authorNotes: Do NOT add on Forms 7, 7A, 30. Place in the section where the date is printed (often the last declaration row, not always the signature row).

autofill.derivation: Default to the preparation / signing date; editable.

truth_declaration.description: The recurring verbatim truth declaration. Reproduce exactly as printed on the specific form (wording varies slightly, e.g. 'information and belief').
truth_declaration.authorNotes: boilerplate with export.verbatim. Adjust the text to the exact words on the form being authored.

snippet.text: The facts and matters stated herein are true to the best of my/our knowledge, information and belief.

hereby_declare_connector.appliesTo: 3, 5, 12, 20, and any form opening 'I/We ... hereby declare:'
hereby_declare_connector.description: The short 'hereby declare:' connector that closes the applicant line and opens the declaration.
hereby_declare_connector.authorNotes: Share the opening row's presentation.group so it renders inline after the applicant name.

signature_section.description: The signature section. Set the title to the form's printed signing instruction (e.g. 'To be signed by the applicant or his authorized registered patent agent.').
signature_section.authorNotes: For multi-signature forms (1, 5) use signature_block_grouped instead of, or in addition to, this.

snippet.title: To be signed by the applicant or his authorized registered patent agent.

signatory_section.appliesTo: all forms that print 'Name of the natural person who has signed'
signatory_section.description: The signatory-name section. Autofill prefers the authorised agent's name (Form 26) then the Form 1 signatory.

snippet.title: Name of the natural person who has signed.

fields.label: Name of the natural person who has signed

signatory_with_designation.description: Signatory name plus designation, and an optional official seal. Drop the official_seal field except on Forms 26 and 30.
signatory_with_designation.authorNotes: Drop into the signatory section's fields[]. Keep official_seal only where the form prints 'official seal, if any'.

snippet.label: Name of the natural person who has signed

signature_block_grouped.description: A signatureBlock grouping signature + name + date, repeatable — for forms with several distinct signing points.
signature_block_grouped.authorNotes: One uniform construct: list several of these (renamed) for each printed signing point. Add a 'capacity' child only if the form distinguishes applicant vs agent explicitly.

addressee_section.appliesTo: all forms EXCEPT 28 (which prints no addressee)
addressee_section.description: The 'To, The Controller of Patents, The Patent Office, at ...' footer with the jurisdictional office dropdown.
addressee_section.authorNotes: Do NOT add on Form 28. The four offices are fixed. Autofill derives the office from the applicant's address / the office recorded on Form 1.

fields.text:
To
The Controller of Patents,
The Patent Office,
at

autofill.derivation: Jurisdictional patent office based on the applicant's address or the office recorded on Form 1.

office_use_header.description: The read-only 'FOR OFFICE USE ONLY' header block the Patent Office completes. Reproduced on preview but never editable by the applicant.
office_use_header.authorNotes: On Forms 18 and 18A the first field is 'RQ No.' not 'Application No.' — rename accordingly. No autofill (office-allotted).
